description: The Caribbean Drought Bulletin of the Caribbean Regional Climate Centre at the Caribbean Institute for Meteorology and Hydrology tracks how dry spells or droughts, and to a lesser extent excessive rainfall, have developed over the past few months and up to a year. Each bulletin details drought situations at regional and national levels for one, three, six and twelve month periods, with short- and long-term drought outlooks, drought alert maps and headlines on drought impacts on the region's climate-sensitive sectors. Bulletins are issued monthly (September 2026 was the latest on the page read) with an archive back to at least January 2020, and the centre also publishes bulletins for agriculture, coral reef health and tourism, a Caribbean climate database and a climate impacts database. Access is free and public; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: the bulletins are documents with maps, not gridded data files, and some months are missing from the list. Coverage is the Caribbean. It supports drought hazard exposure and climate adaptation planning for water supply, hydropower and agriculture on the islands; related records are the global drought hazard SPEI return periods and the NEA Georgia hydrometeorological services.
